movement_source: row 'Total impairment (charges)/benefits', column Full Year Sept 2024 -> column Full Year Sept 2025
headline: WBC's credit impairment charge fell $113m in FY25, from $537m in FY24 to $424m in FY25 (5 bps of average loans, down from 7 bps). The lower charge was mainly due to an increase in write-backs and recoveries partly offset by a higher CAP charge. By provision type: new IAPs fell $15m, write-backs and recoveries rose $159m (benefit), CAP write-offs rose $75m, and other changes in CAP rose $14m (benefit). By division (A$): Consumer fell $31m to $217m (from $248m), Business & Wealth rose $103m to $245m (from $142m), Institutional swung from a $120m charge to a $1m benefit, New Zealand swung from a $25m charge to a $41m benefit, and Group Businesses rose $2m to $4m (from $2m). The investor pack's FY24–FY25 net profit bridge corroborates the total, showing impairment charges contributing +$113m to net profit.

drivers.columns: Full Year Sept 2025 minus Full Year Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: New IAPs fell from $423m to $408m, mostly in the services and wholesale & retail trade sectors and the mortgages portfolio. Where it arose: Business & Wealth's charge rose $103m to $245m (from $142m) reflecting higher overlays, an increase in the downside scenario and new IAPs in the wholesale & retail trade sector; Institutional's $1m benefit (vs $120m charge) was partly offset by new IAPs within the service sector.

drivers.columns: Full Year Sept 2025 minus Full Year Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: Write-backs rose from $93m to $195m and recoveries from $190m to $247m; recoveries mostly within credit cards and personal loan portfolios, write-backs mostly in wholesale & retail trade and manufacturing. The bank says the lower charge was mainly due to an increase in write-backs and recoveries partly offset by a higher CAP charge. Where it arose: New Zealand's benefit of $41m (A$, vs $25m charge) was driven by write-backs and a CAP benefit, largely in mortgages.

drivers.columns: Full Year Sept 2025 minus Full Year Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: CAP write-offs rose from $486m to $561m, largely within the credit card and personal loan portfolios. Where it arose: Consumer's charge fell $31m to $217m (from $248m), reflecting write-offs in cards and personal lending and an increase in the downside scenario weight, partly offset by a release of portfolio overlay provisions.

drivers.columns: Full Year Sept 2025 minus Full Year Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: Other changes in CAP benefit rose from $89m to $103m, driven by an improved economic outlook for commercial property prices and interest rates, a reduction in mortgage 90+ day delinquencies from 1.05% to 0.70%, an increase in the downside scenario weight of 5pp reflecting geopolitical instability, and an increase for new portfolio overlays. Where it arose: Institutional's benefit driven by revisions to economic forecasts; New Zealand's CAP benefit in mortgages; Consumer's release of portfolio overlay provisions.

disagreements.topic: Investor pack page 49 impairment composition chart comparison
disagreements.explanation: The chart's start and end labels are 2H24 and 2H25, so it describes the half-on-half movement, not the FY24→FY25 task comparison. The results announcement page 21 table with explicit FY25 and FY24 columns is the primary framing.
Page 45 states the benefit in NZ$; the segment table on page 33 reports New Zealand in A$.

limitations: The investor pack page 49 impairment composition chart is a half-on-half (2H24→2H25) walk, not the FY24→FY25 comparison; its bars (New IAPs +251, Write-backs & recoveries -238, Write-offs direct +282, Other movements in CAP -27) describe the half-on-half movement and were not used as contributions to the FY25-vs-FY24 bridge. The primary framing is the results announcement page 21 provision-type table, which carries the exact FY25 and FY24 columns.

Segment reporting in FY25 was revised for compositional changes (merchant services moved from Business & Wealth to Institutional; auto finance from Business & Wealth to Group Businesses); FY24 comparatives have not been restated, so divisional deltas partly reflect these changes. The group total is unaffected.
New Zealand's impairment benefit is stated as $44m in NZ$ (page 45) versus $41m in A$ (page 33 segment table); the A$ figure is used in the divisional where-layer.

The 'other changes in CAP' driver combines asset-quality improvements (economic outlook, delinquencies) with overlay and downside-scenario increases; the bank does not split the $14m benefit between these sub-drivers.
Basis normalised from 'cash' to 'ex_notables': no page in evidence prints 'cash' beside the movement, and the registry names ex_notables as the bank's headline basis.
